item.title: Purse found of woman, 24, swept from California beach three weeks ago
item.description:
Se Nah Park was overwhelmed by a wave at the notorious Panther Beach

The purse of a 24-year-old who was swept into the ocean at a notorious California beach three weeks ago was found on Wednesday, as the west coast saw record high king tides.

The Santa Cruz county sheriff’s office confirmed that Se Nah Park’s purse was found by a beachgoer at 4 Mile Beach, south of Panther Beach, where she was swept away into the ocean on 8 November.

item.title: The explosion of extreme wealth is the major problem of our time | Bernie Sanders
item.description:
At this pivotal moment in American history, let us move forward together to take on and defeat a powerful, greedy and corrupt ruling class

We are at a pivotal moment in history. Never before in human history have so few people held so much wealth and so much power. And never before have we seen such an unprecedented level of greed, arrogance and irresponsibility on the part of the world’s ruling class.

Here is the good news: leaders from around the world are finally starting to wake up. This week, elected officials and economists from around the world – including four Nobel prize winners – came together in Paris for a “Summit Against International Oligarchy”. As the summit’s proclamation stated, “The explosion of extreme wealth is the major social fact of our time … We are sounding the alarm: billionaires are a threat to our democracies.”

Bernie Sanders is a US senator, and ranking member of the health, education, labor and pensions committee. He represents the state of Vermont and is the longest-serving independent in the history of Congress

item.title: The US army just detonated a poison bomb over Iowa | Steven Donziger
item.description:
The shocking situation in Iowa is a metaphor for much of what is wrong with the United States

There’s no way to hide it: the US government just deliberately detonated a poison bomb of lead azide over the state of Iowa when a totally safe alternative was available.

The problem in Iowa was relatively simple to solve. The army for decades had stored lead underground at a munitions facility. As far back as 2009, the government knew the lead was deteriorating and might blow up on its own. But it procrastinated. Finally, in March, the army hired a Georgia-based company to use a chemical spray to neutralize the lead, creating a non-hazardous byproduct that can be disposed of in landfills.

Steven Donziger is a US-based human rights and environmental lawyer and the author of Donziger On Justice on Substack
